title: Gate Dispersive Charge Detection in Ge/SiGe Quantum Dots
authors: M. R. Tanvir, E. Sajadi, M. Veldhorst, G. Scappucci, J. Salfi
abstract: Spin qubits are an attractive platform for scalable quantum information processing, and recently, laterally gated quantum dots (QDs) in Ge heterostructures have emerged as a leading implementation of spin qubits. To date, RF single-hole transistors (SHT) and integrated superconducting resonators have been used for spin and charge readout, but their size can pose challenges. Here we demonstrate compact RF gate-dispersive charge readout of a Ge double QD (DQD), and a single hole box (SHB)-DQD system. We resolve QD loading and interdot transitions with both techniques. We find that the SHB enhances the interdot signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of our 540 MHz circuit by a factor of 20 for a DQD coupling $t_c \approx 5$ GHz, providing a unity-SNR at 135 microseconds, c.f. for 2.7 miliseconds for the direct detection. Power- and temperature-dependent measurements verify that SNR is limited by dielectric loss which compromises impedance matching. These results establish a compact readout approach based on gate-dispersive detection for Ge/SiGe heterostructure QDs.
summary: This paper demonstrates a novel, compact method for reading out charge states in Ge/SiGe quantum dot qubits using RF gate-dispersive detection. By integrating an auxiliary localized quantum dot (SHB), the authors significantly boost the signal-to-noise ratio for detecting interdot charge transitions. This establishes a powerful, scalable readout approach for solid-state spin qubits.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing compact and high-fidelity readout methods for spin qubits implemented in Ge/SiGe quantum dots.
main_result: The incorporation of an auxiliary localized quantum dot (SHB) enhances the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for detecting interdot transitions by a factor of 20 compared to direct gate-dispersive readout.
method: The authors employed RF gate-dispersive (GD) charge readout, comparing it against standard SHT measurements, and optimizing the readout using an auxiliary dot.
model_or_system: The system is a laterally gated Double Quantum Dot (DQD) fabricated in Ge/SiGe heterostructures, augmented with a Single Hole Box (SHB) acting as an auxiliary localized QD state.
key_observables: Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), RF amplitude/phase response, and charge transition lines on stability diagrams.
important_parameters: DQD coupling strength ($t_c \approx 5$ GHz), measurement time ($t_m$), and operating temperature (down to 10 mK).
main_assumptions: The SNR is ultimately limited by dielectric loss, which compromises impedance matching at higher power levels.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the measurement circuit schematic, stability diagrams showing DQD and SHB resonances, and plots detailing the temperature and RF power dependence of the RF-GD response.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for compact readout, demonstrating the RF-GD technique, quantifying the SNR enhancement provided by the SHB, and finally analyzing the dependence of the readout signal on temperature and RF power.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses scalable quantum hardware by presenting a robust, compact readout mechanism crucial for characterizing and controlling spin qubits, which is central to quantum computing.
